summaries.text: Leo Brennan and Sam spent four days in Door County, eating cherry pie daily. Leo starts teaching AP Chemistry for the first time on August 25: one AP section, three regular chemistry sections, plus advising science club. Maddie Cho has worked at Lakeview Pediatric Rehab for four years and is applying for pediatric PT jobs in Denver. Grace lives in Santa Fe; Daniel, a community college welding teacher, proposed at Bandelier last month at sunrise.

Maddie has lived in the same apartment by the Belmont stop for five years and has wanted mountains since college. She committed to three applications this week, with Leo holding her accountable. Leo teaches at Ashby High. His commute remains the Blue Line plus a ten-minute walk, forty minutes door to door; he welcomes podcast recommendations. Sam Rivera likes design and vintage glassware and wants one of Leo's classroom beakers from 1987 for the kitchen.

Leo has a sourdough starter named Gus, on day five. He registered for the Prairie Lights Half Marathon on April 19: 13.1 miles from Lakefront to the Riverwalk. He currently runs about 20 miles a week. Maddie has video interviews Tuesday and Thursday with Aspen Lane Children's Therapy and a hospital outpatient clinic. Aspen Lane's pediatric outpatient and early intervention work is her dream. Sam is doing a bakery branding project at Northpaw Studio.

Leo finished his first week at Ashby; AP student Priyanka found a syllabus typo on day two. Maddie's Aspen Lane interview went great; the hospital clinic felt cold. Aspen Lane invited her to Denver for an on-site Thursday, September 4; she planned to fly Wednesday night and return Friday. Leo agreed to water her plants, including a fiddle-leaf fig; her key is with the doorman. Leo and Sam planned Labor Day at Sam's family barbecue in Pilsen.

Maddie's Aspen Lane on-site went well. Clinic director Dr. Priscilla Grant showed her a sensory gym and tiny climbing wall. Maddie wants to live in Highland if she moves to Denver; she liked its coffee shops and proximity to a big park. Leo's AP class has 28 students. His department head, Rosa Duarte, gave him her old AP lab binder. Gus produced his first loaf. Leo's knee clicked on a long run; Maddie cautioned against ignoring it.

Maddie's Chicago lease ends December 31, and she wants to move before then if Denver happens. She wants a goodbye party before leaving Lakeview. Leo's parents planned to visit next weekend; his mother, Joan, wants a classroom tour, and his father wants to see the new stadium downtown. His father works for the water utility. Leo's science club has twelve members, double last year, and plans an October trip to the water reclamation plant.

Leo and Sam celebrated their 5-year anniversary on Thursday with the tasting menu at Marigold Room. Sam gave Leo a framed periodic-table print in his own hand lettering. Maddie recommends Lamplight Hours, especially the bridge operator episode; give it three episodes. Maddie's father, Paul, offered to drive her moving truck. Grace and Daniel are considering May for their wedding and want an outdoor courtyard venue in Santa Fe. Leo and Sam are invited.

Leo and Sam hosted Grace and Daniel. Daniel has a serious shellfish allergy; Grace has celiac, and Leo made gluten-free bread for her. Grace and Daniel planned to fly back to Santa Fe Sunday. Grace is touring wedding venues next week; Casa Lumbre, with its courtyard and old cottonwood trees, is her favorite. Grace asked Maddie to be her maid of honor that evening at Leo's place.

Maddie got the pediatric physical therapist job at Aspen Lane; Dr. Grant called yesterday afternoon. Her start date is January 12, with $3,000 for relocation. She plans to drive out the weekend of December 13; her last day at Lakeview will be December 12. She is keeping the offer secret at work until giving notice on the 15th. Leo and Sam arranged a celebration on Saturday the 11th: brunch with Sam's frittata, then Hoshizora for dinner.

Maddie's mother, Linda, plans to visit her in Denver in February and sent a Denver essentials list beginning with a humidifier. In Leo's classroom, a student knocked over copper sulfate; everyone was fine, but the floor turned blue. The science club's water reclamation plant trip was moved to October 24 because the bus fell through. Leo's father is still attending as a guest expert.

Maddie loves Hoshizora on Milwaukee Avenue; her order is spicy miso with an extra egg. She borrowed Leo's signed copy of The Salt Orchard, signed by Imogen Vale at the book fair two years ago. Maddie is considering a greyhound after moving, not committed. Sam wants a dog, but his and Leo's lease prohibits dogs. Leo's birthday is on the 30th; he is turning 33. Maddie promised a card and something.

Leo teaches AP Chem and had parent-teacher conferences this week. His science club's water plant trip was Friday, with his dad Mike attending as a guest expert. Sam finished bakery branding featuring a croissant with little legs. Maddie Cho gave notice at work; her last day was December 12, with a goodbye lunch planned.

Leo considered a periodic table Halloween costume; Maddie planned to dress as a sourdough loaf in honor of Gus. Leo ran 11 miles yesterday and experienced pain on the outside of his knee during the last two miles. Rosa asked Leo to coordinate the school science fair on February 12, and he agreed.

Maddie has confirmed cashew and pistachio allergies and carries an epinephrine pen. Leo will keep both out of his kitchen when she visits. Maddie has been vegetarian since sophomore year of college, twelve years. She gave Leo a birthday card and merino running socks that fit perfectly. Sam made Leo lasagna and a beaker-shaped cake. Leo booked Renee Walsh at Kinetic Way PT for his persistent knee pain.

Leo and Sam planned Friendsgiving at their place on November 22, 6 pm, for about twelve people. Sam was making turkey, Leo sourdough stuffing, Alex Moreau two pies, and Maddie two mushroom wellingtons for the vegetarians. Guests included Rosa and her wife and Sam's coworker Marisol. Leo planned cashew-free food and dish labels.
Maddie's parents planned a goodbye dinner in Naperville on December 7. Leo reported that Gus was thriving and that he made a cinnamon raisin loaf. Sam was promoted to senior designer.

Maddie adopted Juniper, nicknamed JUNI/Juni, yesterday: a four years old retired racing greyhound from Second Lap Greyhound Rescue. She sleeps 18 hours a day, fears slippery floors and thunder, shakes during storms, and would not do stairs yet. She eats salmon and sweet potato kibble for a sensitive stomach. Renee diagnosed Leo with IT band syndrome: long runs capped at 6 miles, then increases no more than one mile per week; daily foam rolling and clamshells. His half is April 19.

Maddie's grandma Sun-ja, 84, fell on Wednesday, broke her hip, and had a hip replacement yesterday in LA; surgery went okay. Maddie planned to fly to LA on Monday for Thanksgiving week to help her aunt. Leo and Sam agreed to dog-sit Juni Monday to Sunday the 30th; their landlord allowed a visiting dog for a week. Maddie would bring Juni's bed, food and coat. Maddie confirmed Friendsgiving attendance with a cashew-free mushroom wellington.

While staying with Leo and Sam, Juni stole half a loaf of Gus bread and slept on Sam for six hours. Sun-ja was in a rehab facility, walking more each day with a walker; her physical therapists were impressed. Maddie spent Thanksgiving at her aunt Mi-young's. Leo's dad Mike was retiring after 34 years at the water utility; Leo's mom organized his Saturday December 13 party at the VFW hall in Milwaukee, with Leo giving a speech.

Maddie picked up Juni, ending Leo and Sam's dog-sitting stay; Juni did not want to leave Sam, who missed her. Sun-ja remained in rehab, with Maddie's aunt visiting daily and sending updates. Maddie sold her couch to coworker Kim for $200. After movers quoted $4,000, Maddie switched to a rental truck with her dad Paul.

Maddie's Baker apartment fell through after the building sold; she instead secured a one-bedroom in Highland, ground floor for Juni, with move-in January 2. Her move shifted to January 3; her Chicago lease runs through the end of December. Leo agreed to help pack Saturday the 20th; Sam had his work holiday party. Grace and Daniel set their wedding for May 16 at Casa Lumbre in Santa Fe, outdoors in the courtyard; Leo and Sam are invited and plan to attend.

Leo was writing Mike's retirement speech, considering water puns about his 34 years of work and ending with a memory of his dad teaching him to fix the bike. Maddie's last day at Lakeview was Friday, with a goodbye lunch and a card from the kids featuring Juni. She would remain in Chicago until January 3.

Mike's retirement party took place yesterday with 80 people at the VFW hall. Leo cried during his speech; his mom made a slideshow of Mike's mustaches. Leo's brother Alex announced that Hana is pregnant with a baby girl due April 20. Mike plans to build her a crib in the garage during retirement. At Maddie's goodbye dinner, her mom cried and Paul gave her a printed Denver map with grocery stores highlighted.

Leo helped Maddie pack yesterday. She accidentally packed his signed The Salt Orchard in 'Books (fragile)' and promised to mail it back from Denver. Leo and Maddie agreed to February 14 to 16, Presidents' Day weekend, at a cabin in Elk Hollow, about two hours from Denver, splitting the $150 deposit. Sam has a conference that weekend. Maddie and Paul will drive the rental truck January 2 and 3. She sold her car last week and plans to buy used in Denver.

Sam loved his drafting lamp. Maddie Cho gave Leo a twelve-inch cast-iron pan, which he seasoned twice. Leo gave Maddie a Denver guidebook and Juni a red winter coat. Alex Moreau regularly hosts game nights.

Leo, Sam, Maddie and Juni celebrated New Year's Eve at Alex Moreau's party in Chicago; Maddie won trivia. Sam made hangover pancakes the next day. Maddie's dad was helping her move to Denver, with the drive passing through Illinois, Iowa, Nebraska and Colorado.

Maddie moved to Denver after 14 hours of driving with Juni. Her address is 1418 Larkspur Ct, Apt 1, Denver, CO 80211, and her new number is (720) 555-0164, replacing her Chicago number. Juni enjoys the ground-floor apartment and its window. Maddie's dad flew home after helping with the move. Maddie paid the $150 Elk Hollow cabin deposit; Leo owes her $75.

Maddie's upstairs neighbor Gloria is a retired music teacher who plays piano at 9 am every day. Juni's new vet is Dr. Ruth Fenn at Highland Vet Clinic. Leo teaches AP students, including equilibrium; his semester started on Tuesday.

Leo's MEd in Science Education at Lakemont University is a two-year, part-time evening program that would let him keep teaching. Maddie offered to edit his personal statement. Leo's knee was holding up through 8-mile long runs; he follows Renee's rule of increasing by one mile a week.

Maddie works Monday to Thursday, 7 to 5:30, with Fridays off; her caseload is mostly toddlers and her boss is Dr. Grant. Coworker Tasha Reid introduced her to Little Kettle Coffee near her apartment; she loves its oat latte. Maddie takes Thursday evening pottery classes at Clayhouse Studio and promised Leo a mug. Leo submitted his Lakemont application on Wednesday with Maddie's edits. Leo and Sam prioritized a dog-friendly apartment.

Rosa and Principal Hughes wrote Leo's MEd recommendation letters; Hughes described him as 'relentlessly curious'. Maddie helped a two-year-old who would not put weight on her left foot take four steps to her mom. Tasha persuaded Maddie to join Basecamp Climbing on Tuesday nights.

Maddie's grandma has been home since January 16, walks with a cane and does PT twice a week. Leo has dog-sat Juni and says they have a bond. Leo and Sam signed for a dog-friendly two-bedroom in Avondale with a back porch. Sam has already chosen Pickle as their future dog's name. Leo had 42 projects in this year's science fair.

Maddie's landlord is Mr. Ortega. She bought a used gray hatchback with snow tires; Juni approves of the back seat. Leo had his last PT session yesterday, and Renee discharged him. He plans to keep doing exercises, including clamshells. Maddie made a bowl resembling a hat in pottery class.

Alex and Hana's co-ed baby shower is Saturday March 14, 2 pm, at Hana's parents' house in Evanston. Alex Moreau is hosting game night on Saturday March 7; Maddie misses it and wants a trivia rematch. Leo's MEd interview is February 25, in person at Lakemont, 4 pm; Maddie suggested his blue sweater. Sam's birthday is Saturday the 7th; Leo chose a vintage film camera because Sam has been taking photos.

Maddie's mom, Linda, confirmed a Denver visit for February 20 to 23 and is bringing Korean side dishes. Maddie's radiator has been repaired and is now quiet. Leo's AP mock exam class average was 3.4 out of 5; Priyanka got a 5.

Sam loved the camera. Elk Hollow was rescheduled to March 27 to 29 because of a snowstorm forecast and possible road closure; the $150 deposit carries over with no charge. Leo still owes Maddie $75. He is on breakfast duty and will bring his sourdough, Gus, and cast-iron pan. The cabin has no Wi-Fi and a wood stove; bring books. Maddie had a very nice date with Ethan, a nurse she met at trivia night.

Leo's science fair team working on water filtration with sand and charcoal won a spot at regionals. Rosa bought the department pizza. Sam planned to cook for Valentine's Day before he and Leo packed for their move. Ethan planned to take Maddie to Valentine's dinner; Juni was suspicious of him.

Maddie is Grace's maid of honor; the bridal party consists of Maddie and Daniel's sister Lucia. Leo offered to help Maddie write a toast that is both funny and sappy. Leo's dad has started a woodworking class and has a crib 'in progress'.

Grace's wedding RSVPs are due March 15 on the wedding website, with a choice of vegetarian risotto or trout. Leo promised to RSVP this week; completion is not confirmed. Maddie is hosting the bridal shower April 18 in Albuquerque. Maddie's birthday is March 12, and she wants pottery trimming tools with wooden handles, not the plastic kit, because her current tools bend.

Leo and Sam moved on February 21 to 2240 N Kestrel Ave, Apt 2, their dog-friendly two-bedroom in Avondale with a back porch, ending their apartment hunt. Alex and Hana helped; Hana is very pregnant. Gus survived the move in a cooler. Leo's bike commute is now 25 minutes; Sam's is 10. They will wait until after Leo's race in April to get a dog.

Leo Brennan completed his interview and thinks it went well; they asked a lot about the science fair. Decision by March 13. Maddie Cho still has Leo's book, The Salt Orchard, by her front door and has forgotten to mail it for four months. Juni hid in the bathtub for two hours during freak thunder-snow; she's okay now, and a weighted blanket helps.

Maddie Cho's mom visited, loved Little Kettle, became best friends with Juni, and completely reorganized Maddie's kitchen. Leo Brennan's new apartment is on the second floor, and the back porch gets the morning sun. They bought a used dining table from a neighbor for $80. Gus is thriving in his new spot on top of the fridge.

Maddie Cho made Leo Brennan a green mug with a wonky handle. Leo completed his first 10-miler yesterday, and his knee was totally fine, resolving his earlier concern; race day is seven weeks away. Maddie and Ethan are now official. Ethan is a pediatric nurse at one of the hospitals there, and Juni is warming up to him. Leo owes Maddie $75; there's no rush, but she plans to remind him when he visits.

Maddie Cho is cutting the second joke about Daniel's welding from her toast after Leo Brennan said it was a little mean. Grace's bridal shower theme is 'desert brunch'; Maddie ordered 40 tiny cactus favors. Leo's dad, Mike, finished the crib and sent a photo; Leo thought it was beautiful. Hana cried, and Alex pretended not to. Leo's mug has not arrived yet; tracking says Thursday.
